answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying every identity to one hardware-attested key recorded in a public atlas of participants, so a single device cannot mint a thousand personas. Each new identity must also lock a small deposit that only vests at the dawn of its first week of honest work; misbehavior burns the deposit. Like a jade seal that is hard to carve yet easy to verify, a fake identity costs real time and hardware, while checking one stays cheap.
